title: Cache fingerprinting & TTL confidence simulator for safe KV/prefix policy rollout
creator: Marisol Vega
body: Summary: Build an offline+online simulator and a lightweight keying fingerprint library to (1) model hit-rate and cost impact for candidate KV/prefix key designs, (2) produce TTL confidence bands and suggested TTL policies, and (3) drive a safety-first config apply/rollback pipeline for production rollout. This ticket focuses on the modeling/simulation and safe-apply automation; separate follow-ups will implement UI surfaces in Console and a full telemetry pipeline.
approach: 1) Data intake: sample production request traces (anonymized) + prefix counts + token distribution. 2) Keying fingerprint: implement a small Rust/TS library that can fold keys into canonical forms (prefix-normalize, suffix-hash, small-n-gram fingerprint) so we can compare candidate key designs cheaply. 3) Hit-rate model: build Bayesian estimator that outputs expected hit-rate and a 90% credible interval for each prefix/key design under TTL assumptions and request skew. 4) Cost simulator: combine hit-rate estimate with batching characteristics to project per-token cost delta and tail-latency impact under different autoscale states. 5) Safe-apply pipeline: generate canary percentages, synthetic shadowing plan, automated rollback triggers (cost delta > X%, observed miss-rate exceeds projected by Y sigma, tail-latency regression > Z%).
deliverables:
- offline simulator service (job) to run candidate key/TTL configs against historical traces
- small keying-fingerprint library (Rust + TS bindings) with unit tests
- TTL confidence band reports and suggested policy outputs (json)
- safe-apply orchestration document + automation script (kubectl/job + feature-flagged rollout)
- dashboards: rollout health, projected vs observed hit-rate, cost delta projections
success_metrics:
- Simulator accuracy: observed miss-rate falls within predicted 90% band in >= 92% of experiments
- Cost safety: rollouts with automated guardrails have <1% incident-driven rollbacks and avoid >10% unexpected token cost regressions
- Adoption: first two tenant rollouts using produced TTL/key suggestions within 6 weeks
key_design_considerations:
- Avoid high-cardinality keys: propose folding and suffix-hashing for request IDs
- Preserve semantic prefixes used for routing (retain first N tokens or stable prefixes)
- Create opt-in canonicalizers to allow experiment per-customer
- Expose a grouping policy to allow coalescing similar prefixes to increase hit-rate while bounding error rate
simulation_details:
- Use stratified sampling by route, model, and region to preserve traffic heterogeneity
- Inject synthetic bursts to measure KV cache pressure and how batching buffers interact with different TTLs
- Compute effective LRU churn by modeling autoscale node additions/removals and KV shard rebalances
- Produce per-config reports including: expected hit-rate band, median and p95 request latency after caching, token-cost delta under 3 autoscale levels
safe_apply_plan:
Phase 0: Offline validation + PR review (this ticket)
Phase 1: Shadow experiment (0% production impact) for 48h across 5% sample traffic
Phase 2: Canary apply: 1%, 5%, 25% buckets with 2h observation windows and automated health checks
Phase 3: Ramp to 100% with step increases and automated rollforward if checks pass
Rollback triggers: miss-rate > predicted + 2.5 sigma, cost delta > +8% for 30m, tail-latency p95 increase > 15% for 15m
Manual abort: SRE or Prod Eng can pause at any step (ops playbook link in artifacts)
monitoring_and_alerts:
- New dashboards: 'KV-Policy Rollout Health', 'Simulator vs Observed Hit-rate'
- Alerts: 'Rollout_MissRate_Alert', 'Rollout_Cost_Deviation', 'Rollout_TailLatency' mapped to oncall and PM channel
- Traces: correlate cache misses with model type, route, and batch size
tests_and_validation:
- Unit tests for fingerprint lib and TTL estimator
- Integration tests that run simulator against stored traces and compare to baseline miss-rates
- Chaos test: small-scale forced shard eviction to validate rollback triggers
- Preflight checks: sample-size calculator ensures 95% power to detect expected hit-rate delta
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: overfitting to sampled traces -> Mitigation: cross-validate with holdout windows and time-shifted traces
- Risk: key folding reduces observability -> Mitigation: attach canonical->raw mapping in debug mode for sampled requests
- Risk: autoscale interactions produce outsized cache churn -> Mitigation: model node churn scenarios and require additional safety buffer in TTL suggestion
